text: Given a mocked vendor GET /api/Packages response with two packages, When msp360_list_packages is called, Then the response has count: 2, two package entries each with exactly package_id/name/cost/storage_limit_gb/restore_limit_gb/enabled, and has_more: false.

Given a mocked vendor GET /api/Packages response with zero packages, When msp360_list_packages is called, Then the response is {"packages": [], "count": 0, "has_more": false} and not an error envelope.

Given the vendor login call (POST /api/Provider/Login) returns 401, When msp360_list_packages is called, Then the result is {"error": {"code": "unauthorized", "retryable": false, ...}} and the mocked GET /api/Packages client is never invoked.

Given the request to the MCP server is missing the X-Msp360-Username header, When msp360_list_packages is called, Then the server responds with an auth failure listing the required headers, and no HTTP call to MSP360 is made.

Given two concurrent requests with different credentials (tenant A's mocked vendor response returns package "Starter", tenant B's returns package "Enterprise"), When msp360_list_packages is called for each, Then tenant A's result contains only "Starter" and tenant B's only "Enterprise", with no cross-tenant mixing.

Given a mocked vendor 200 login response containing a distinctive access_token value, When msp360_list_packages is called and its response body and all captured log output are searched for that exact string, Then the string is not found anywhere.
Given a mocked vendor response with 60 packages, When msp360_list_packages() is called with no arguments, Then exactly 50 are returned and has_more: true.
Given a mocked vendor response with 60 packages, When msp360_list_packages(limit=200) is called, Then all 60 are returned and has_more: false.
Given a mocked vendor response with 250 packages, When msp360_list_packages(limit=500) is called, Then at most 200 are returned (the hard cap wins over the requested limit) and has_more: true.

Given the GET /api/Packages call times out or returns a 5xx response, When msp360_list_packages is called, Then the result is {"error": {"code": "upstream_error", "retryable": true, ...}} and not an unhandled exception.

Given a mocked vendor response containing one package with Enabled=true and one with Enabled=false, When msp360_list_packages is called, Then both packages are returned (neither is filtered out) and each entry's enabled field correctly reflects its own vendor status.
